tips.title: Two-Cut Method with GodHand SPN-120 Nippers
tips.text: GodHand SPN-120 Ultimate Nippers have razor-sharp edges that leave almost no stress mark, but they are fragile and will chip if used on thick gates. Use the two-cut method: first cut the gate 2mm from the part with cheaper nippers (Tamiya 74123), then make the final flush cut with the GodHand. Never twist or pull the part off — always cut straight through. This works especially well on delicate Eduard photo-etch frets and Clear Prop Models canopy parts.

tips.title: Scribing Panel Lines with RB Productions Panel Line Scribing Tool
tips.text: RB Productions panel line scribing tool creates precise, consistent panel lines with minimal effort. Set the tool to 0.1mm for 1/72 scale, and apply light pressure while moving the tool evenly across the surface. This prevents plastic deformation and ensures sharp, clean lines. Use with Tamiya 74123 or GodHand nippers to remove excess plastic after scribing. Avoid using Mad Mike tools for detailed work on thin plastic as they can cause surface cracks.

tips.title: Photo-etch Bending Jigs for ICM and Eduard Parts
tips.text: Use ICM or Eduard photo-etch bending jigs to form delicate metal parts without bending them out of shape. Place the part on the jig, align it with the pre-drilled holes, and apply gentle pressure using pliers. For ICM parts, use a 2mm jig; for Eduard, use a 1.5mm jig. Always bend slowly and avoid over-stretching the metal to maintain structural integrity and prevent breakage.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning with Iwata Airbrush Cleaner
tips.text: Clean Iwata airbrush needles with Iwata Airbrush Cleaner (100ml bottle) after each use. Soak the needle in the cleaner for 5 minutes, then use a soft brush to remove residue. For stubborn buildup, use a 0.3mm brass cleaning rod. Never use alcohol or ammonia-based cleaners as they can damage the needle’s surface and reduce paint flow. Always replace the needle after 50 hours of use to maintain precision.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya Tape vs Kabuki Tape
tips.text: Tamiya Masking Tape (12mm width) is ideal for masking large areas on plastic models due to its strong adhesive and ease of removal. Kabuki Tape (6mm width) is better for small, detailed areas like wingtips or engine cowls. Apply Tamiya tape with a squeegee to avoid bubbles, and use Kabuki tape with a small brush for tight spaces. Both tapes can be dissolved with Tamiya Masking Tape Remover, but Kabuki requires a bit more effort to lift without damaging the paint layer.
